event: Israel announced it killed Mohamed Odeh, described as Hamas's military chief, 11 days after his predecessor was killed.

verified_facts.statement: Israel announced the killing of Mohamed Odeh, described as a senior Hamas military commander.
verified_facts.note: Standard IDF announcement format; name and title are primary-record facts.

verified_facts.statement: Odeh's killing occurred 11 days after his predecessor was killed.
verified_facts.note: Temporal relationship stated in event; verifiable against dated announcements of both operations.

verified_facts.statement: The October 7, 2023 attack on Israel resulted in approximately 1,200 Israeli deaths.
verified_facts.note: Widely documented Israeli government figure; primary-record casualty count.

verified_facts.statement: An October 2025 ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas was nominally in effect at the time of Odeh's killing.
verified_facts.note: Verifiable against dated ceasefire announcements; existence of agreement is factual, though terms are disputed.

verified_facts.statement: The strike that killed Odeh struck a residential building in a populated Gaza neighborhood.
verified_facts.note: Confirmed by multiple sources (IDF, Hamas, media); location type is concrete fact.

verified_facts.statement: Odeh's wife and children were killed in the strike.
verified_facts.note: Reported by Hamas, IDF, and international media; family deaths are verifiable primary facts.

verified_facts.statement: The strike occurred on or near Eid al-Adha.
verified_facts.note: Eid al-Adha 2025 date is fixed; timing of strike relative to holiday is verifiable.

verified_facts.statement: Cumulative Palestinian deaths since October 2023 have been reported at over 72,800.
verified_facts.note: Gaza Ministry of Health figure; widely cited but disputed in methodology by some sources.

verified_facts.statement: Post-ceasefire Palestinian deaths have been reported at over 900.
verified_facts.note: Reported by Palestinian health authorities and international monitors; specific count varies by source and date.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Odeh was possibly the last pre-war senior Hamas council member remaining in Gaza.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Requires verification of Hamas organizational structure before October 2023 and current status of all members; no single authoritative source confirms this claim.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Odeh had a direct operational role in planning the October 7 attack.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Israeli intelligence assessment; not independently verified by third parties; Hamas has not publicly confirmed or denied specific roles.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Netanyahu issued a simultaneous order to seize 70% of Gaza.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Reported by some sources but not confirmed by official Israeli government statement; exact percentage and timing disputed.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: The ceasefire agreement contains a suspension clause allowing resumption of hostilities.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Reported in media accounts but full text of agreement not publicly released; exact terms remain opaque.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Phase 2 ceasefire talks are deadlocked specifically over Hamas disarmament.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Reported by multiple sources but neither Israel nor Hamas has released official negotiating positions; characterization of 'deadlock' is interpretive.

points_of_disagreement: Whether Odeh's killing constitutes legitimate retributive justice vs. an extrajudicial execution or war crime.
Whether the October 2025 ceasefire was in effect and whether the strike violated it.
Whether the strike's civilian casualties were proportionate to the military advantage gained.
Whether Odeh retained targetable status under international humanitarian law during a ceasefire.
Whether the killing advances or undermines the path to a durable peace settlement.
Whether Hamas's military organization is collapsing or merely adapting.
Whether Gazan civilians support or oppose Hamas leadership.
Whether Israel's decapitation strategy is strategically effective in achieving its stated objectives.
Whether the strike was operationally precise or reckless in its targeting methodology.
shared_foundation.summary: All framings accept that Israel killed Mohamed Odeh, a senior Hamas military commander, in a strike on a residential building that also killed his family members, 11 days after his predecessor's death, during a nominally active October 2025 ceasefire. The disagreements concern the legality, legitimacy, strategic wisdom, and humanitarian cost of the operation—and whether it advances or sabotages the peace process.

framings.name: Justified Accountability / October 7 Justice
framings.question: Is Israel lawfully and morally entitled to hunt down and kill every architect of the October 7 massacre?
framings.key_claim: The killing of Odeh is legitimate retributive justice — Israel is systematically eliminating the perpetrators of the deadliest attack on Jews since the Holocaust, as promised.
framings.description: This framing treats targeted killings of Hamas military leadership as both morally warranted and strategically necessary, anchoring every strike to October 7. It foregrounds Odeh's direct role in planning the massacre and frames the campaign as Israel keeping its sworn promise to survivors.
framings.emphasizes: Odeh's direct role in October 7 planning; IDF/Shin Bet operational precision; Israel's stated vow to reach every perpetrator; the Oct. 7 death toll of ~1,200 Israelis
framings.downplays: Collateral civilian deaths in the strike; ceasefire-compliance questions; whether killings advance peace negotiations
sample_headlines: The fourth commander of the Hamas terror organization's military wing in Gaza was eliminated and sent to meet his partners in the depths of hell — Israel Katz
Israel kills Hamas military wing chief Mohammed Odeh in Gaza airstrike

carriers.name: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu / Defense Minister Israel Katz (joint statement)
carriers.excerpt: "We will continue to pursue everyone who took part in the October 7 massacre. Sooner or later, Israel will reach them all."
carriers.role_evidence: Netanyahu and Katz jointly coined and launched this framing in the immediate post-strike announcement, defining Odeh explicitly as 'one of the architects of the October 7 massacre.'

carriers.name: Fox News Digital
carriers.excerpt: "Almost nobody remains from the core group that planned and led the October 7 attack," analyst Michael Milshtein told Fox News Digital.
carriers.role_evidence: Led US right-leaning audience coverage with the 'Israel hunts Oct. 7 terrorists' frame, amplifying the accountability narrative to a large national audience.

carriers.name: Times of Israel
carriers.excerpt: "The security agencies described Odeh as one of the last remaining senior Hamas military commanders involved in orchestrating the October 7 massacre."
carriers.role_evidence: Provided the most detailed early English-language reporting grounding the accountability frame in IDF/Shin Bet sourcing.

carriers.name: FDD's Long War Journal (Foundation for Defense of Democracies)
carriers.excerpt: "The rapidity of the second decapitation strike was predicated on months of IDF and Shin Bet tracking of Odeh and his network."
carriers.role_evidence: Policy-think-tank outlet amplified the accountability-plus-operational-success framing, contextualizing Odeh's killing within a broader documented Israeli targeting campaign.

framings.name: Ceasefire Violation / Rule-of-Law Critique
framings.question: Does Israel's campaign of targeted killings during an active ceasefire constitute a violation of the truce and international law?
framings.key_claim: Striking Odeh while a ceasefire nominally remains in effect is part of a systematic Israeli pattern of violating the October 2025 truce and undermining any path to peace.
framings.description: This framing treats the killing not as a discrete counterterrorism operation but as evidence that Israel is waging war under the cover of a formal truce. It foregrounds the ~900 Palestinians killed since the October ceasefire and legal arguments about whether IHL targeting rules permit post-ceasefire strikes.
framings.emphasizes: Civilian deaths since the October 2025 ceasefire; Hamas's description of the killings as 'extrajudicial executions'; the ceasefire agreement's suspension clause; destruction of a residential building
framings.downplays: Odeh's specific Oct. 7 role; Hamas's own ceasefire violations; Israel's legal arguments that armed conflict continues
sample_headlines: Since last October's so-called U.S.-brokered ceasefire, Israel has killed some 900 Palestinians in Gaza
Hamas accused Israel of 'nothing but an extension of the policy of extrajudicial executions'

carriers.name: Hamas (official statement)
carriers.excerpt: Hamas labeled the campaign "nothing but an extension of the policy of extrajudicial executions and systematic killing."
carriers.role_evidence: Hamas's official statement upon confirming Odeh's death explicitly framed the killing as illegal extrajudicial execution, establishing this counter-narrative.

carriers.name: Democracy Now!
carriers.excerpt: Gaza City resident on air: "There is no ceasefire. Day and night, there is shelling."
carriers.role_evidence: Amplified the ceasefire-violation framing by centering a Gazan resident's direct testimony, framing the strike as part of ongoing unlawful bombardment.

carriers.name: Genocide Watch
carriers.excerpt: "Such claims have allowed Israel to continue violating the ceasefire with impunity, using alleged Hamas violations as justifications for its own actions."
carriers.role_evidence: Published a formal special report cataloguing Israeli ceasefire violations and framing the targeting campaigns as systematic IHL breaches, lending institutional weight to the critique.

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: "Israel responded to the October 7 attack by launching a genocidal war against Palestinians in Gaza, killing more than 72,800 people."
carriers.role_evidence: Reached a global English-language audience; embedded the killing within the ceasefire-violation and civilian-harm framing in its primary news report.

carriers.name: Just Security (Michael Schmitt & Ryan Goodman)
carriers.excerpt: "The ceasefire agreement provides, 'All military operations, including aerial and artillery bombardment and targeting operations, will be suspended.'"
carriers.role_evidence: Provided a rigorous legal analysis distinguishing what LOAC permits from what the ceasefire text prohibits — complicating but engaging both the Israeli legal justification and the ceasefire-violation critique.

framings.name: Human Cost / Civilian Harm
framings.question: Who else died or was harmed in the strike, and what is the cumulative toll on Gaza's civilian population?
framings.key_claim: Beyond the targeted commander, the strike killed Odeh's wife, children, and bystanders inside a residential building in a populated neighborhood, adding to a post-ceasefire toll that has surpassed 900 Palestinian deaths.
framings.description: This framing centers the verified deaths of non-combatants — Odeh's wife, two to three children, and at least three to six additional people wounded or killed — and situates the strike within a broader pattern of civilian casualties across Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire.
framings.emphasizes: Family deaths; destruction of a residential apartment building; neighborhood disruption on Eid al-Adha; 72,800+ cumulative Palestinian deaths since October 2023
framings.downplays: Odeh's command role and operational threat; Hamas's own use of civilian spaces as hideouts
sample_headlines: Hamas confirms military chief Mohammed Odeh killed by Israel, along with his wife and two of his children
Gaza health officials said six people, including at least one woman, were killed and more than 20 others were wounded in the same Israeli strike

carriers.name: NBC News
carriers.excerpt: "Gaza health officials said six people, including at least one woman, were killed and more than 20 others were wounded in the same Israeli strike."
carriers.role_evidence: One of the first major US outlets to lead with health-official casualty numbers alongside the targeted killing announcement, centering the civilian harm framing.

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English (Hind Khoudary, field reporter)
carriers.excerpt: Khoudary reported "a lot of destruction" after the attack targeted "a busy neighbourhood of the city as residents were preparing for the Eid al-Adha holiday."
carriers.role_evidence: Field reporting from Gaza City foregrounded the human cost and timing (Eid holiday) of the strike, making civilian harm viscerally concrete for international audiences.

carriers.name: Human Rights Watch
carriers.excerpt: "Throughout the year, Israeli war crimes and crimes against humanity, including of apartheid and persecution, against Palestinians have persisted."
carriers.role_evidence: HRW's World Report 2026 established the institutional human-cost baseline into which individual strikes like the Odeh killing are folded by advocates and journalists.

carriers.name: UN OHCHR (Ajith Sunghay statement)
carriers.excerpt: "The Israeli military has killed 72,769 Palestinians since 7 October 2023 in Gaza: in their homes, in IDP shelters, in hospitals, in schools."
carriers.role_evidence: The UN human rights chief's contemporaneous statement provided the authoritative international institutional voice for the cumulative civilian harm framing.

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour / AP (via PBS)
carriers.excerpt: "Israel's retaliatory strikes have killed more than 72,700 people, according to the Gaza Health Ministry."
carriers.role_evidence: Repeated the Gaza health ministry casualty figures prominently, contextualizing each individual strike within the broader population-level harm narrative.

framings.name: Strategic Effectiveness / Decapitation Debate
framings.question: Does killing successive Hamas military chiefs actually degrade the organization, or does it merely accelerate leadership rotation without ending the conflict?
framings.key_claim: While Israel's intelligence-driven decapitation campaign is operationally impressive, expert analysis suggests it is unlikely, on its own, to force Hamas to disarm or end the Gaza impasse.
framings.description: This is an analytical, expert-driven framing that asks whether targeted killings of leaders produce durable strategic gains. It weighs Israel's clear operational capability against Hamas's demonstrated organizational resilience and warns that removing experienced leaders may produce more radical successors.
framings.emphasizes: Hamas's demonstrated resilience; risk that newer leaders may be more extreme; the need for a political strategy to accompany military action; ACLED and Carnegie expert assessments
framings.downplays: Moral or legal dimensions; the immediate security threat Odeh represented
sample_headlines: Israel has killed 2 Hamas military leaders this month. But will it change the underlying conflict?
Israel's killing of another 2 Hamas leaders is unlikely to break Gaza deadlock. Here's why.

carriers.name: Boston Globe
carriers.excerpt: "While targeted killings may provide tangible achievements that leaders can brand as victories, they rarely address the underlying grievances that propel conflicts."
carriers.role_evidence: Published one of the first US analytical explainers specifically interrogating the strategic efficacy question for the Odeh/Haddad double killing.

carriers.name: Washington Times / AP wire (Nasser Khdour, ACLED)
carriers.excerpt: "The killing of senior commanders is unlikely, on its own, to push Hamas toward disarmament or make it accept the complete removal of its role in Gaza."
carriers.role_evidence: AP analysis distributed across major outlets, carrying ACLED and Carnegie expert skepticism to a broad US readership.

carriers.name: ACLED (Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project)
carriers.excerpt: "Despite its losses, Hamas' military wing has remained resilient" and the timing "suggests Israel's effort to raise the cost of refusing disarmament."
carriers.role_evidence: Provided the authoritative data-driven expert comment grounding the strategic-efficacy skepticism, quoted by AP and multiple outlets.

carriers.name: Mohanad Hage Ali (Carnegie Middle East Center)
carriers.excerpt: "You can decapitate an organization or defeat it militarily, but if you don't follow through politically, it doesn't work."
carriers.role_evidence: Carnegie Middle East Center analyst's quote was widely reproduced, anchoring the 'decapitation without political strategy is insufficient' argument.

carriers.name: Fox News Digital (Michael Milshtein, Palestinian arena expert)
carriers.excerpt: "The people replacing them are far less experienced, less capable and far less charismatic," but Hamas "continues to maintain functioning chains of command."
carriers.role_evidence: A right-leaning outlet nonetheless included expert strategic skepticism, demonstrating the framing's cross-spectrum presence.

framings.name: Hamas Organizational Collapse / Survival
framings.question: Has Israel's serial decapitation campaign brought Hamas to the verge of organizational collapse, or is the group adapting and surviving?
framings.key_claim: With Odeh — possibly the last pre-war senior council member in Gaza — now dead, Hamas is transforming from a coherent military organization into a smaller, fragmented militia fighting for survival.
framings.description: This framing focuses narrowly on Hamas's organizational state: its shrinking leadership pool, deteriorating command-and-control, and competition from other armed factions. It is distinct from the 'effectiveness debate' framing by emphasizing evidence of Hamas's actual degradation rather than the theoretical limits of decapitation.
framings.emphasizes: Odeh as possibly the last pre-war core council member; growing disconnect between Hamas leaders and Gazan civilians; Hamas described as 'fighting for survival'
framings.downplays: Hamas's stated ideological resolve; the group's continued territorial control of ~half of Gaza; civilian harm in the strikes
sample_headlines: Hamas struggles to fill leadership ranks as Israel hunts Oct. 7 terrorists
'Hamas is now fighting for survival' — analyst Hadeel Oueis, Jusoor News

carriers.name: Hadeel Oueis / Jusoor News (via Fox News Digital)
carriers.excerpt: "With the deaths of its leaders and the collapse of strong centralized command, Hamas is turning into a smaller militia competing with other armed groups."
carriers.role_evidence: Jusoor News editor coined the sharpest organizational-collapse framing, first quoted in this form by Fox News Digital.

carriers.name: Fox News Digital
carriers.excerpt: "Hamas is now fighting for survival."
carriers.role_evidence: Distributed the organizational-collapse framing to a large US conservative audience, pairing it with Gaza street footage showing little civilian mourning for Odeh.

carriers.name: FDD Long War Journal (Samuel Ben-Ur)
carriers.excerpt: "Odeh was the second-to-last member of Hamas's core council in Gaza, leaving only Imad Aqel."
carriers.role_evidence: FDD analyst provided the granular organizational mapping — identifying the narrowing leadership bench — that gave the collapse framing its empirical backbone.

carriers.name: SOFX (military/special operations outlet)
carriers.excerpt: "He is the fourth commander of the Qassam Brigades eliminated by Israel since the October 7, 2023, attack."
carriers.role_evidence: Specialized military outlet used a sequential 'fourth commander' frame that implicitly supports the organizational-degradation narrative.

framings.name: Ceasefire & Peace Process Damage
framings.question: How does the killing of successive Hamas military chiefs affect the fragile ceasefire and the stalled second-phase peace negotiations?
framings.key_claim: Israel's continued targeted killings are accelerating the breakdown of the October 2025 ceasefire at precisely the moment that the peace process is stalled over Hamas disarmament, making a durable settlement harder to reach.
framings.description: This framing situates the Odeh killing within the political logic of the Gaza peace process — noting that both Israel and Hamas have accused each other of ceasefire violations, that the second phase of the deal is deadlocked, and that killings signal Israel's prioritization of military pressure over diplomatic progress.
framings.emphasizes: Fragile ceasefire; deadlocked Phase 2 talks; Hamas's refusal to disarm; Netanyahu's simultaneous order to seize 70% of Gaza; mutual accusations of violations
framings.downplays: Odeh's operational threat; moral questions about October 7 accountability
sample_headlines: Israel and Hamas are deadlocked in indirect talks over implementing the second phase of a ceasefire deal, which includes the group's disarmament
These territorial moves come after Hamas rejected the International Board of Peace's directive to disarm

carriers.name: NBC News
carriers.excerpt: "Israel and Hamas are deadlocked in indirect talks over implementing the second phase of a ceasefire deal, which includes the group's disarmament and Israeli army withdrawals."
carriers.role_evidence: Foregrounded the peace-process-damage angle by placing the killing explicitly within the stalled Phase 2 negotiating context.

carriers.name: CBC News
carriers.excerpt: "Hamas described him as a central figure in directing combat operations and accused Israel of trying to achieve politically through killings what it had failed to achieve militarily."
carriers.role_evidence: On the predecessor killing, CBC foregrounded Hamas's framing that Israel is pursuing political goals through military means — directly implicating the peace process.

carriers.name: FDD Long War Journal
carriers.excerpt: "These territorial moves come after Hamas rejected the International Board of Peace's directive to disarm, a key condition of US President Donald Trump's 20-point peace plan for Gaza."
carriers.role_evidence: Placed the killing within the Trump peace plan framework, linking the military campaign to Israeli leverage over the disarmament impasse.

carriers.name: ACLED (Nasser Khdour)
carriers.excerpt: "The timing also suggests Israel's effort to weaken Hamas' control in Gaza and raise the cost of refusing disarmament."
carriers.role_evidence: ACLED analyst explicitly linked the timing of the killing to Israel's negotiating leverage strategy, making the peace-process-damage framing analytically credible.

framings.name: Gaza Civilian Resilience / Hamas Disconnect
framings.question: What do the reactions of ordinary Gazans — not Hamas officials — reveal about the relationship between the group's military leadership and the civilian population?
framings.key_claim: Gazan civilians went about Eid celebrations hours after Odeh's killing, with some expressing relief or indifference, revealing a deep rift between Hamas's military leadership and a population exhausted by nearly three years of war.
framings.description: This framing uses on-the-ground reporting to surface an under-covered perspective: ordinary Gazans' ambivalence or quiet relief at Hamas leaders' deaths, driven by resentment at being 'volunteered for martyrdom.' It sits outside the standard pro-Israel/pro-Palestinian binary.
framings.emphasizes: Crowded Eid markets hours after the strike; anonymous Gazan testimony blaming Hamas for civilian suffering; Hamas-civilian disconnect; growing grassroots anti-Hamas sentiment
framings.downplays: Israeli military's role in Gaza's destruction; questions about whether Israel is the cause of civilian suffering
sample_headlines: Palestinians shop at a crowded Eid al-Adha market in Gaza hours after Israel announced the killing of Mohammed Odeh
'Ordinary people are the ones who paid the price, not the leaders who made reckless decisions' — anonymous Gaza activist

carriers.name: Fox News Digital (field reporting from Gaza, citing Jusoor News activists)
carriers.excerpt: "Ordinary people are the ones who paid the price, not the leaders who made reckless decisions without thinking," the activist said.
carriers.role_evidence: Exclusively surfaced anonymous Gazan civilian testimony on the Hamas-civilian disconnect, pioneering this framing in US coverage of the Odeh killing.

carriers.name: Hadeel Oueis / Jusoor News
carriers.excerpt: "Hamas did not only hurt the Israelis — they hurt us as well" — Gaza human rights advocate quoted by Jusoor News.
carriers.role_evidence: Jusoor News, a regional outlet, gathered the civilian testimony that gave the framing its primary source material.

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour (Hussein Ibish on Sinwar killing, contextual)
carriers.excerpt: "In Gaza, interestingly, there's a significant group of people who appear to be delighted with his passing, because they blame him rightly for having volunteered the entire population for martyrdom."
carriers.role_evidence: PBS NewsHour gave this civilian-resentment angle mainstream legitimacy in the Sinwar context; its framing was directly recycled in Odeh coverage.

framings.name: International Law / LOAC Targeting Legitimacy
framings.question: Does the Law of Armed Conflict permit Israel to conduct lethal targeting operations during a formal ceasefire, and is the 'preventive vs. punitive' distinction legally sound?
framings.key_claim: The legality of killing Odeh under international humanitarian law turns on unresolved questions about whether the conflict persists through a ceasefire, whether Odeh retained targetable status, and whether the strike satisfied proportionality requirements.
framings.description: A specialist academic-legal framing that breaks the targeting question away from moral and political debates and into technical IHL/LOAC analysis. It scrutinizes whether a ceasefire suspends armed conflict for targeting purposes, the distinction between preventive and punitive killing, and whether the residential-building strike met the precaution and proportionality requirements.
framings.emphasizes: IHL status of ceasefire vs. armed conflict; IDF International Law Division's 'preventive' targeting doctrine; proportionality and precaution obligations; the distinction between criminal accountability and LOAC targetability
framings.downplays: Political context; moral arguments about Oct. 7 justice; civilian casualty numbers as a standalone metric
sample_headlines: 'Hunting' the October 7 Attackers: What the Law of Armed Conflict Permits — and What It Doesn't
A ceasefire, standing alone, is but a temporary suspension of hostilities — Just Security analysis

carriers.name: Just Security (Prof. Michael Schmitt, University of Reading; Prof. Ryan Goodman, NYU Law)
carriers.excerpt: "It is also essential to understand that the LOAC targeting rules apply to the Israeli campaign against the Oct. 7 attackers even though there has been a ceasefire."
carriers.role_evidence: The most detailed US-published IHL legal analysis of Israel's post-ceasefire targeting campaign, originating this specialist framing with reference to Odeh's killing specifically.

carriers.name: OHCHR / UN Human Rights Office (Ajith Sunghay)
carriers.excerpt: The OHCHR report "documents large-scale violations of international law, including atrocity crimes, and points to war crimes and possible crimes against humanity."
carriers.role_evidence: UN's principal human rights body formally adopted a legal-violation framing for the broader campaign within which the Odeh strike falls.

carriers.name: Human Rights Watch
carriers.excerpt: "The IDF has regularly violated the principle of proportionality, carrying out military actions which lead to damage and civilian impact that would far outweigh the military advantage gained."
carriers.role_evidence: HRW's World Report 2026 established the institutional IHL-violation baseline that advocates apply to individual strikes, including the Odeh killing.

carriers.name: Genocide Watch (special report)
carriers.excerpt: "The IDF has regularly violated the principle of proportionality, carrying out military actions which lead to damage and civilian impact that would far outweigh the military advantage gained."
carriers.role_evidence: Published a contemporaneous legal-analysis report on ceasefire violations that directly informs the IHL framing around post-ceasefire strikes like the Odeh killing.

gap_analysis: Missing: the operational/tactical perspective from Israeli security officials on specific intelligence, targeting methodology, and how this fits into broader military strategy beyond just 'decapitation.' Missing: voices from regional actors (Egypt, Qatar, other Arab states) on implications for mediation efforts and their own strategic interests. Missing: the internal Hamas succession/power dynamics framing—who replaces him, does this create factional instability or consolidate control? Missing: the civilian-in-Gaza economic/governance angle—how does loss of military leadership affect Hamas's ability to provide services, security, or maintain order in territory it controls.

coverage_lean.event: Israel announced it killed Mohamed Odeh, described as Hamas's military chief, 11 days after his predecessor was killed.

matched.carrier: Washington Times / AP wire (Nasser Khdour, ACLED)

coalition.structure_note: 7 of 21 actors actively champion more than one framing (real cross-cutting, not just broad coverage); see the bridges and any contested actors for who connects — or splits — which lenses.
